newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-WARNE HELPS AUSTRALIA SQUARE ONE-DAY SERIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WARNE HELPS AUSTRALIA SQUARE ONE-DAY SERIES.

text.p: Two wickets in successive overs from leg-spinner Shane Warne helped Australia to level their seven-match one-day series against South Africa at 2-2 with a 15-run victory on Saturday.
Warne removed Daryll Cullinan for 38 and opener Adam Bacher for 45 to put the skids under a South African chase for 212 in the fourth game which began promisingly.

Seamer Andy Bichel then strangled the South African middle order with figures of three for 43 and, although man-of-the-match Shaun Pollock struck 41 not out to give his team a fighting chance in the closing overs, Australia squared the series with 11 deliveries to spare.

South Africa had recovered from the early loss of opener Herschelle Gibbs for no score and appeared to be heading for a comfortable victory as Bacher and Cullinan shared in a second-wicket stand of 80 in 24 overs.
Both batsmen were helped by a dropped catch apiece by Adam Gilchrist at first slip but wrist-spinner Warne then triggered the collapse as South Africa lost four wickets for just eight runs.
Warne first removed Cullinan and Bacher. Jonty Rhodes was yorked for one by a Jason Gillespie inswinger and Jacques Kallis was run out for one by Steve Waugh.

Captain Hansie Cronje (28) and Derek Crookes (17) regrouped with a sixth-wicket partnership of 36 but South Africa's most likely chance of snatching victory lay with Pollock's 10th-wicket assault of 36 runs in only three overs with Allan Donald.
Earlier, Pollock took career-best figures of four for 33 as Australia were restricted to 211 for nine in their 50 overs.
Although opener Greg Blewett made a solid 53 and Gilchrist a pugnacious 77, Australia were always under considerable pressure from accurate South African bowling backed up by some superb fielding.

Gilchrist, in only his fifth limited-overs international, struck five fours and two sixes and added 42 with Andy Bichel for the eighth wicket before on-driving Pollock to South African captain Hansie Cronje at mid-wicket.
